Read by BOTH providers.ts and providers.py. Two loaders reading one file cannot drift, and
four repositories reading the same SHAPE of file cannot fork.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY BYTE-IDENTICAL, checked with cmp rather than asserted. micro-brand's copy of
this file claims providers.py, compare.py and verify.py are byte-identical across the estate;
that claim is false and is being corrected there. compare.py is identical NOWHERE — the
difference is real logic, not a header line. So this file states only what a reader can check:
probe.ts                differs by ONE LINE: a usage example that named a provider id this
registry no longer has. `--provider qwen-image-2512` is now a hard
`unknown provider` exit, and a documented command that cannot run is
the rot this header exists to prevent. Nothing else in it changed.
backends.ts             BYTE-IDENTICAL AGAIN, and the round trip is worth recording because
it is the argument for the seam, settled by events rather than
asserted. When Qwen-Image 2512 was withdrawn this file's OpenAI-shaped
images envelope was deleted here along with the transposed-`size`
compensation that existed only for that endpoint's bug, and this
header said the siblings still carried it and would need the same
removal. A second model is on trial now, so the envelope is BACK — as
a NEW implementation of the same vendor shape, probed from scratch,
with no workaround in it, because none of the eleven probes behind
`openaiImagesBackend` found a reason for one. Adding gpt-image-2 cost
one registry entry, one member on `AdapterKind`, one backend and a
native-size path in generate.ts — against the rewrite it would have
been had the seam been collapsed back to one hardcoded model.
WHAT WAS KEPT THROUGHOUT is the DETECTION rather than the workaround:
generate.ts still measures every delivered non-square image against
what the BACKEND asked for and refuses to keep a transpose, for any
provider. That is the guard that would have caught the bug in the
first place, and it is not specific to the model that had it.

replay.ts, dialects.json, dialects.py, dialects.ts,

history costs three repositories a diff and buys nothing. The

compare.py, verify.py,  deliberately different here, and each difference is named. verify.py

where the siblings are reference-only, which is what makes this the

Only verify.py's check_parity is genuinely shared, not the whole file.
The rule the estate actually wants is not sameness, it is that a DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE AND
SAID SO. An unexamined copy that has silently drifted is the thing to avoid, and asserting
sameness that stopped being true is how that happens.
LAYOUT. The reference provider's root is the repository itself: its assets are at assets/ and
its provenance is MANIFEST.json. That is a requirement rather than an aesthetic choice —
MANIFEST.json records a `path` for every entry, CI globs assets/**/*.png, and moving the
reference set to sets/flux/ to make the roots look alike would rewrite every one of those
paths in all four repositories.
So the challengers go under candidates/<id>/, which also states the truth: the reference set is
SHIPPED and a challenger is on trial. If a challenger wins it is promoted by moving its tree to
assets/, and the `provider` field on each entry records which model the shipped bytes came from.
ONE MANIFEST PER SET, not one merged manifest. Regenerating a candidate must never rewrite the
file that holds the reference set's provenance, and a candidate set is expected to be RED for
most of this exercise while the reference stays green. verify.py takes --provider and reads
exactly one manifest, so those two states do not collide.
$identity: How an asset is identified in THIS repository's manifests. The one thing that genuinely
differs between the estate's asset repositories: micro-brand keys on surface + kind, and the
three game sets key on a single dotted `asset` path such as objects/seating-stool.
Naming it here rather than in code is what keeps the LOADERS free of a hardcoded key, which

the rest differ only where a difference was chosen. See the header for what is actually

providers.vendor: Black Forest Labs, served by Azure AI Foundry

billing.source: request_meta.cost on each response, recorded per asset as providerCostUnits

notes: Cost is NOT flat per image: 3 units up to roughly 1MP, 4.5 measured at 1920x768.
Delivered dimensions floor to a multiple of 16, which is why requestSizeFor rounds up.
Every declared size in this repository is already a multiple of 16 EXCEPT the two derived
title cards (1200x630 and 1600x900), which are cropped from compliant generations and
never requested. See docs/ecosystem/23-tessera.md §2.1.
Accepts no seed parameter, so `seed` is null on every entry rather than invented. That
absence is why Tessera authors ONE canonical facing per object and mirrors the second at
render time: a pipeline that cannot fix a seed cannot render the same chair four times.

providers.label: GPT Image 2
providers.vendor: OpenAI, served by Azure AI Foundry (AIServices S0, Sweden Central)

billing.source: usage.output_tokens on each response, recorded per asset as providerCostUnits

notes: WHY THE DIALECT IS `literal` AND NOT `positive`, which is the only real choice in this
entry. `positive` was not written as a general improvement to the house style. It was
written against ONE measured failure of ONE model: Qwen-Image 2512 demonstrably received
the prohibitions in full and disregarded them while honouring the positives. No such
measurement exists for this model, and until one does, generating it in `positive` would
confound two variables at once — different model AND different brief — in the one
comparison whose entire value is that only one thing changes. So this set replays the
reference record byte for byte, and COMPARISON.md's question stays 'which model is better
on identical input'.
AND IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN ANY SIBLING, because of what this repository's prompts
still carry. generate.ts's header says so: the hardening clause aimed at Qwen's MEASURED
failures — the recursive picture-frame grid and the Hokusai pastiche — is still in every
one of the 288 recorded prompts, because it is what the shipped set was generated from and
stripping it would make the manifest unreproducible. A `literal` challenger therefore
inherits a brief that was hardened against a model that is not it. That is a real
asymmetry, it is NOT a reason to reword the prompts under a second model, and COMPARISON.md
must state it rather than let a reader discover it in the prompt column.
THE WIRE, MEASURED, in micro-brand, against this same deployment and this same key, before
a single asset of that set was generated. It is restated rather than cross-referenced
because a fact that lives in another repository is a fact nobody reads. Nothing below is
off a model card.
* `api-key: <key>`, not `Authorization: Bearer`.
* Body `{model, prompt, size, n, quality}`. `model` must be `gpt-image-2` and must be in
the body even though the route is an OpenAI-compatible one — the same trap the
reference provider sets, arrived at from the other direction.
* The response carries `b64_json` ONLY. There is no `url` field, so there is no download
step and no expiring link to race.
* PNG is the default. FLUX returns JPEG unless asked; this does not, so `output_format`
is not sent.
* `background: "transparent"` is REFUSED: 400 image_generation_user_error. AND THAT IS
NOT IRRELEVANT HERE, unlike in the three sibling repositories. This is the only set in
the estate that ships a real alpha channel: the 40 avatar overlays are cut by cutout.py
and verify.py check 8a fails a plate with no transparency. The cut is done numerically
from the flat ground either way, for both providers alike, so nothing about the
comparison changes — but a reader who sees `background` refused should know the answer
was 'it was never going to be asked for' rather than 'nobody noticed'.
* `seed` is REFUSED: 400 unknown_parameter. So `seed` is null on every entry in this set,
exactly as it is on every FLUX entry, and for the same reason: nothing true can be
recorded. doc 23 §2.1 turns on that fact — a pipeline that cannot fix a seed cannot
render the same chair four times, which is why Tessera authors one canonical facing and
mirrors the second at render time. Both models share the constraint, so it changes
nothing about the comparison and everything about the title.
* C2PA is PRESENT on every delivered PNG. Measured on the bytes by `measureC2pa`, never
inherited from this paragraph.
THE SIZE CONTRACT, BISECTED, AND IT COSTS THIS SET MORE THAN ANY OTHER IN THE ESTATE. Two
rules: both dimensions divisible by 16, and a MINIMUM PIXEL BUDGET in (524288, 655360] —
1024x512 is refused and 1024x640 is accepted. Above the budget, arbitrary sizes are
honoured exactly, so this deployment is NOT limited to the three sizes the OpenAI images
API documents.
TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY-NINE of this set's 288 generations fall UNDER that budget — 80% of
it, against 76% in micro-aetherholm-assets, 25% in micro-emberkin-assets and 4% in
micro-brand. The reason is what this game is: a 1x1 seed object occupies one 256x128 tile
on screen, so it is authored at 512x512, and there are 132 sprites at that size before the
48 avatar plates and 40 glyphs are counted. Each is asked for at the smallest exact-aspect
multiple on the 16-grid that clears the budget and is Lanczos-downscaled to the declared
size:
512x512  → x2   → 1024x1024  (132: 96 objects, 24 structure, 12 markers)
256x512  → x2.5 →  640x1280  (48: the avatar plates and overlays)
256x256  → x3.5 →   896x896  (40: 24 glyphs, 16 economy icons)
768x768  → x1.5 → 1152x1152 (8: the kiln sheets)
1024x512  → x1.5 → 1536x768  (1: the wide chrome mark)
The 768x768 kiln sheets are the interesting row: 589,824 px sits INSIDE the unmeasured gap
between refused and accepted, so backends.ts treats it as refused and scales. That is the
conservative direction on purpose — guessing the other way costs a 400 on every asset of a
kind for the length of a run, and guessing this way costs tokens.
Nothing is upscaled anywhere. The as-delivered native is kept at
candidates/gpt-image-2/native/<set>/, OUTSIDE assets/, so verify.py's orphan walk and
materialise.py never see it, and its checksum, size and C2PA state are recorded on the
asset's own row and re-measured by verify.py's `check_native`. That last part is the whole
guarantee: without it, 'generated at 512x512' is a sentence nobody has compared to a file.
AND THE DOWNSCALE INTERACTS WITH THIS TITLE'S ONE UNREPAIRABLE FAILURE, WHICH IS WHY THE
DIRECTION IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. COMPARISON.md §1b calls a sprite drawn out of the
2:1 dimetric projection *unusable* rather than merely worse — the single adherence failure
in this set with no downstream repair. A Lanczos downscale is an affine operation on an
existing grid and cannot move a vanishing point or a viewing height, so a sprite that came
back in projection is still in projection at 512. An upscale would invent the very edges
the projection is read off, which is why verify.py's check_native treats a native smaller
than its declared size as a failure rather than a note.
WHAT THE DOWNSCALE DOES COST is detail budget, and the glyphs are the sharp end: a 256x256
glyph drawn as an 896x896 picture has 12.25 times the area to put detail in, and detail
that survives at 896 and dies at 256 is exactly the failure mode of an icon that COMPARISON
.md §3 judges at 16 and 24 pixels. If this set's small chrome reads busier or muddier than
the reference's, the downscale is the FIRST thing to suspect and not the model.
CONCURRENCY 1, AND THAT IS NOT CAUTION. Two back-to-back requests returned 429
RateLimitReached, 'Please retry after 32 seconds'. This is a shared S0 quota, not dedicated
hardware, so fanning out makes a run slower rather than faster: every parallel request that
429s still costs its own retry-after. The backend serialises, parses the retry-after out of
the body and honours a Retry-After header. 288 serialised generations is measured in hours.
That is expected and is not a fault.
BILLING IS IN TOKENS, which is a third unit and neither of the two this repository already
had. `usage.output_tokens` is per image and varies with size and quality. It is per-image
accounting like FLUX's cost units, so compare.py takes the per-image path — but the
NUMBERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS PROVIDERS and compare.py must never add them. `basis` is
what it branches on, not `unit`; it used to branch on `unit`, which sent this provider down
the deployment-hour path and asked a serverless endpoint for a DEPLOYMENT.json.
Both env values are read from the gitignored studio/.env.local, which sources them from
~/.config/cloudsforge/azure-images.env (mode 600, outside every repository). Neither value
is ever written to this file, a manifest, a log line, a README, a PR body or a report.

notes: WITHDRAWN, and carried across from the sibling repositories unchanged. The deployment
failed to come up on A100_80GB and has been deleted, so this is a placeholder rather than
a candidate: nothing runs against it and `present()` never returns it, because it has no
manifest.
It is KEPT, and kept complete, on purpose — and it matters more in THIS repository than in
the other three. doc 23 §1 states the constraint Tessera is built around: neither FLUX nor
Qwen emits a mesh, a UV layout, a rig or a frame of animation, so the whole title is
isometric 2D BECAUSE of what these two models cannot do. A third model is therefore a
question of when rather than if, and this entry is the seam it lands in.
deploymentVerified was set from a MEASUREMENT, not from the fact that it looked right.
The three answers that establish it, all with body {"model": "<name>"}:
nvidia--cosmos3-super          -> 400 BadRequestForDependentService (name resolves)
nvidia--cosmos-3-super         -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the NATURAL spelling is wrong)
definitely--not--a--deployment -> 404 DeploymentNotFound (the control)
So a 400 that is not DeploymentNotFound means the gateway reached the model service and
the service rejected our body — which is the good state, and the reason probe.ts keys on
the error CODE rather than on the status.
Every env value above is read from the gitignored studio/.env.local. That file's key is
never written to this file, a manifest, a log line, a README or a report.
